name: HD 1160

planets.name: B
planets.note: Originally classified as a brown dwarf (~33 Mjup) at discovery (Nielsen et al. 2012); later work (e.g. Maire et al. 2016) revised the mass estimate upward, placing it near the stellar/substellar boundary rather than firmly substellar.

extra_papers.title: First light of the VLT planet finder SPHERE. II. The physical properties and the architecture of the young systems PZ Tel and HD 1160 revisited

planets.name: C
planets.note: M3.5 low-mass star (~0.22 Msun), wide companion at ~533 AU; stellar rather than substellar, but included per the discovery paper's own multiplicity finding.

images.wavelength_label: Ks/L'/H/K multi-epoch (2002-2011); common-proper-motion confirmation of B & C
images.credit: Nielsen et al. 2012, Fig. 1 (full 12-epoch tile: VLT NACO + Gemini NICI + Keck NIRC2)

paper.title: The Gemini NICI Planet-Finding Campaign: Discovery of a Multiple System Orbiting the Young A Star HD 1160

images.wavelength_label: L'/Ks multi-epoch (2002-2011); companion C common-proper-motion (seeing-limited; B not detected)
images.credit: Nielsen et al. 2012, Fig. 2 (full VLT ISAAC archival tile)

paper.title: The Gemini NICI Planet-Finding Campaign: Discovery of a Multiple System Orbiting the Young A Star HD 1160

notes: HD 1160 B's classification is disputed (brown dwarf vs. low-mass star near the stellar boundary); HD 1160 C is a confirmed stellar (M3.5) wide companion.
